thread:
Samira (CS): FYI customer James from Acme reporting large score shifts from our rerank endpoint after last deploy. They say same input yields very different ordering and magnitudes. Request ID: req_0a3f. Example attached.

customer-james: Posting the minimal repro we gave them:
```
POST /v1/rerank
{"query":"how to reset password","candidates":["Link A","Link B","Link C"]}
```
Previously top candidate had score 0.82. After your deploy it’s 0.21 and ranking order changed. This started ~2026-02-28 18:23 UTC. Help please — this is impacting search UX.

Samira (CS): They flagged it as P1 and said they saw intermittent 429s earlier today but mostly the symptom now is score instability. They included the old and new raw responses (sanitized):
```
old: {"scores":[0.82,0.47,0.15], "order":[0,1,2]}
new: {"scores":[0.21,0.77,0.10], "order":[1,0,2]}
```

Ethan (ML Eng): @Samira thanks — can you paste the exact rerank model id they hit? Also did they specify rerank-config? We pushed rerank-v3.4.1 to canary this morning, then rolled to 60% at 18:00 UTC. ops-deploy-bot should have the rollout id.

ops-deploy-bot: Deploy started for rerank-service rerank-v3.4.1 by @ci at 1769995200. Canary -> 60% at 1769996400, gradual -> 100% at 1769997000.

Ming (SRE): I'm pulling request logs for req_0a3f now. Samira, did customer include their exact timestamp + request_id? The logs show several retries from the same IP around 18:23.

Priya (Support): I tried reproducing locally with the sample JSON. Using the hosted endpoint with their API key (sanitized) I get:
```
$ curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-***" -d '{"query":"how to reset password","candidates":["Link A","Link B","Link C"]}' | jq .
{"scores":[0.24,0.76,0.12],"order":[1,0,2]}
```
So I can reproduce the new behavior in prod (I used their account region). Verified using their request_id returns same.

Samira (CS): So this is a real regression. Customer expects deterministic-ish scores for identical inputs. They run offline tests comparing rerank output after each deploy.

Ethan (ML Eng): I remember we changed the scorer normalization last week to L2-norm across token embeddings to stabilize long vs short candidates. That patch could rescale scores. But the magnitude change from 0.82 to 0.24 seems large — maybe we also toggled a softmax temperature or introduced logit clipping. I'll diff the model config for v3.4.1 vs previous tag v3.4.0.

Ethan (ML Eng): Quick check: the model artifact metadata for v3.4.1 shows `score_norm: "l2"` and `post_softmax_temp: 1.4` while v3.4.0 had `score_norm: "l1"` and `post_softmax_temp: 0.9`.

Ming (SRE): ETA on reproducer script? I can pull full traces and latency histograms. If retries happened there's a chance clients saw partial responses and retried which could affect aggregated metrics.

Priya (Support): I made a small repro that calls the rerank endpoint 5x in a row with identical payload and prints full JSON each time. Results:
1) {"scores":[0.24,0.76,0.12]}
2) {"scores":[0.23,0.77,0.12]}
3) {"scores":[0.24,0.76,0.12]}
So results are consistent in prod with v3.4.1. Not noisy but shifted.

Ethan (ML Eng): That indicates deterministic behavior post-deploy. Root cause likely model config change. Two avenues: a) roll-back to v3.4.0 for affected customers, b) explain change and provide migration notes + rescore script. We should also check whether normalization change was intentionally part of the release notes. I don't see that in the changelog.

Samira (CS): Customer is asking for immediate rollback or targeted pinning. They have dedicated capacity? They said hosted API. They requested a hotfix or pin to previous reranker for their account.

Ming (SRE): We can create a routing policy to pin that customer to rerank-v3.4.0 within 20 minutes. Need account id and their region. Samira, can you get their account id? Also be mindful of billing — if we pin them and underlying infrastructure differs, usage may spike.

customer-james: Account is acme-corp-73. Please keep me updated. They've also sent a CSV of 2k queries where scores deviate >0.3 compared to our snapshot.

Ethan (ML Eng): I'll run the offline eval on their CSV. If the change was only scale (linear transform) we could provide a temporary score rescaler, but ordering changes mean the model semantics shifted.

Priya (Support): Note — during our checks we saw a few 429s earlier, which were from a spike in retries. Customer also flagged a billing duplicate-charge for retries — can finance investigate? Noting here so it's tracked: billing-incident: BI-592.

Ming (SRE): Logs attached (snip):
```
2026-02-28T18:22:59Z [req_0a3f] 200 OK duration=54ms model=rerank-v3.4.1
2026-02-28T18:23:01Z [req_0a3f] RETRY triggered by client, 429 received from upstream
```
So there were some 429s from an internal helper service at 18:23 that triggered client-side retry. But the primary issue appears to be model config drift, not retries.

Ethan (ML Eng): Offline eval results on 2k queries: 68% of cases show >0.15 absolute score delta, 14% show order inversion relative to v3.4.0. The distribution suggests normalization + temperature caused softmax reweighting making mid-ranked candidates jump above. I can reproduce locally by toggling `post_softmax_temp` from 0.9 to 1.4 and changing `score_norm` from l1 to l2.

Ethan (ML Eng): Proposed mitigation: immediate pin for acme-corp-73 to rerank-v3.4.0 routing + patch & redeploy rerank-v3.4.2 that reverts normalization change and adjusts temperature back to ~0.95. We'll also add an integration test that checks score-change thresholds for a curated anchor set per-customer.

Samira (CS): Customer accepts pinning if we can do it quickly. Please confirm downtime/impact.

Ming (SRE): Pinning route for hosted customers is no-downtime; it's just a routing config change. I'll open a ticket with infra-runbook steps and apply to their account in canary then prod. Will monitor latency/error rates during change. Applying in 10m.

ops-deploy-bot: Routing update applied: account acme-corp-73 pinned to rerank-v3.4.0 at 1769998200. Change by @ming.

Priya (Support): After pinning I re-ran the 3-sample payload. Result now:
```
{"scores":[0.81,0.47,0.14],"order":[0,1,2]}
```
Customer confirms behavior restored for sampled queries.

customer-james: Confirmed for the samples. They're going to run a bulk test and will follow up in 24h. Appreciate the quick pin.

Ethan (ML Eng): I'll ship v3.4.2 with config revert + add the integrational regression check. Also updating release notes to make normalization changes explicit and add a migration guide.

Ming (SRE): I'll loop in billing for BI-592 to check duplicate charges due to retries; support ticket created.

Samira (CS): Thanks team. I'll keep thread open until customer finishes 24h run. After that let's log a postmortem on the release process — we shouldn't change score semantics without a flagged opt-in and evals per major customer.

Priya (Support): Quick action items: 1) Pin customer (done) 2) Run offline eval on CSV (Ethan) 3) Billing check (Ming) 4) Release v3.4.2 revert (Ethan) 5) Add regression tests (Ethan). I'll update the ticket and include repro steps we used.

Ethan (ML Eng): One more note — we should add a per-customer "anchor set" capability in Redwood Console so customers can monitor anchor-query score drift after deploys. Filing a feature request.

Samira (CS): :thumbsup: closing loop once Acme confirms. Thanks everyone.
